User who has been getting into Obsidian and experimenting with chat AIs called Khoj's Obsidian integration excellent; another said it encouraged them to move to Obsidian.

A Khoj developer, sharing results from experimenting with Llama V2/GPT4All in Khoj, said Falcon 7b was not good enough on their machine to be useful. Personal-notes context consumes too many tokens, and the content varies too much for a small model to understand.
User tried searching notes written in Slovene and said it performed very poorly. If the keyword wasn't directly in the note, results seemed more or less random.
Heads up: docker build fails with 'Could not find a version that satisfies the requirement pyside6>=6.5.1 (from khoj-assistant)', and pip install exits with code 1.
User fired up local Khoj on an M2 MacBook Air and it ground the machine to a halt. They compared it to old virus-ridden PCs where the cursor lagged 45 seconds behind the mouse.

Returning user said Khoj was still a bit buggy when they tried it at the previous launch, but was giving it another shot, mainly for local chat. They asked for an easily extended data connector interface for custom sources.
User asked what the PostHog telemetry is used for, noting nothing about it in the docs and no clear way to opt out.
Commenter who saw Khoj 'slaughtered' on HN weeks earlier said messaging is now clearer about current state vs aspirations, with good progress toward the aspirational parts.

User noted the landing page doesn't mention Llama or the offline use case at all, only online use via OpenAI. Separately, another reported the landing page's example prompts cause the page to jump while scrolling on iOS Safari.

User said GPL-3 hurts corporate adoption and asked for non-LLM default search for regular machines. Their current tool is ripgrep-all + fzf, but they want a GUI with multi-folder search, result prioritization and search history.
User who has been trying it: Khoj search does work offline, while Khoj chat is a separate function that requires an OpenAI key and uses OpenAI.

Critics called the 'open-source AI personal assistant' branding misleading because chat relied on OpenAI's GPT API. One said it's 'an OpenAI client that also has something like grep built in'. Another refused to use it because personal data would be sent to ChatGPT.
User looked at the code and said it's a cool project that's clearly had a lot of thought put into it.
User couldn't read the Khoj site on iPhone because the header size kept changing with the typing animation, moving the text up and down every second.
User asked for support for Word documents, saying it doesn't seem to support them yet. Others requested Notion, Gmail/GSuite integrations.
Feature requests from users include Logseq support, PDF directory indexing with OCR for scanned documents, GitLab support, Discord/Google Drive sources, and a Spotlight Search replacement.
